subject: Post-call: inference requirements & next steps — MedicaCore discovery
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.k@azuredge.ai>, Priya Sharma <priya@medcore.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: inference requirements & next steps — MedicaCore discovery

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap while it's fresh and to align on next steps. High-level summary:

- Primary pain: inconsistent interactive latency experienced by customer-facing clinicians when summarizing multi-page patient notes; cost also a concern for heavy nightly batch workflows.
- Goal: ship a hybrid serving setup that gives sub-second interactive responses for short chat/summary flows (p95 target) while keeping nightly taxonomy and indexing batch jobs cost-effective.
- Key constraints we noted: PHI handling (will likely require Private VPC), average user query ~120 tokens output, typical context window ~2k tokens for full-note summarization, peak concurrent interactive sessions ~60, nightly bulk jobs ~50k docs.

From our side we proposed three parallel items for the deep-dive:
1) Collect a 50-sample prompt set and representative payload sizes (I attached 'medcore-inference-eval-set-50.json').
2) Technical deep-dive to pin p95 latency SLOs and topology options (hosted-dedicated vs private).
3) A short eval run to measure throughput and cost delta between 4-bit quantized model and a standard fp16 variant.

Immediate asks for you:
- Please confirm the PHI requirement and whether a Private VPC is mandatory or optional for the pilot.
- Confirm that the attached sample set is representative or point me to a different sample.
- We suggested a technical follow-up next week — are you available Tue or Wed morning PT?

Attachments referenced: medcore-inference-eval-set-50.json (sample prompts), kv-cache-topology-diagram.png (sketch we drew on the call).

Proposed next steps (we will action on items flagged below once you confirm):
- Schedule a 60-minute technical workshop (Redwood SRE + MedicaCore infra + product).
- Share a preliminary cost/throughput estimate for two topology options. (I attached a rough CSV estimate.)
- Prep a short eval run using your sample prompts.

Thanks —

Ava Chen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.com | (415) 555-0124

Ava / team —

Appreciate the clear notes. Quick answers from our side:
- PHI: Private VPC is required for production; pilot can run in a dedicated-hosted sandbox if we sign a scoped BA/DUA.
- Sample set: the attached 50 prompts are representative of patient-facing queries; thanks. We will add 5 longer edge cases (full discharge summaries) and re-upload to the shared folder by EOD.

Technical clarifications / constraints:
- Interactive target: p95 generation latency <= 350ms for median-length responses (~120 tokens). We realize this will push on model choice / batching.
- Large-context summaries: acceptable p95 up to 1.5s for 2k-token context summarization (nightly job tolerates higher latencies).
- Throughput: steady-state interactive throughput target ~1,200 req/min during peak; nightly batch throughput required ~350 docs/sec (workerized).
- Availability: 99.9% monthly (we can discuss SLA credits with account team).

Questions for Redwood before deep-dive:
1) Do you have a recommended model family for strong summary quality at reasonable cost (our priority: factuality > hallucination suppression)?
2) How do you handle KV cache persistence across short-lived pods to avoid repeated recomputation?

We can do Tue 15 May 10:00 AM PT for the technical workshop (Samir + our infra lead Priya + product).

Thanks,
Samir
Lead Platform Engineer, Azuredge (MedicaCore partner)
samir.k@azuredge.ai

Samir / Priya —

Great — thanks for the targets. I wanted to follow up with concrete topology and model suggestions so we have something to discuss in the workshop. High level recommendations tailored to your constraints:

Option A — Private VPC, dedicated cluster (recommended for PHI):
- Topology: Private control plane managed by Redwood + customer VPC peered nodes. Dedicated GPU fleet behind the VPC (NVIDIA H100 / A100 depending on availability).
- Model: Llama-2-70B or Falcon-40B variant fine-tuned on clinical notes. Quantize to 4-bit QLoRA-style to reduce memory footprint.
- Latency tactics: small pinned replica pool for interactive path, with in-memory KV cache and prefix caching for common templates; per-request continuous batching disabled for interactive route (to preserve latency).
- Autoscale: target warm pool of ~12 interactive replicas to meet 1,200 rpm peak with p95 headroom (we'll run a sim).
- Persistence: short-lived checkpointed KV cache with shared cache store (Redis/Memcached) to hydrate new replicas quickly.
- Nightly bulk: dedicate a separate batch worker pool (higher batch sizes, larger sequence-processing optimized kernels).

Option B — Dedicated-hosted (faster pilot, lower friction):
- Hosted dedicated capacity with strict data handling + contract for scoped PHI pilot. Slightly higher egress risk but faster time-to-value.
- Model and tuning same as A; rely on Redwood-managed KV cache with customer-approved retention/eviction policy.

Evaluation plan for workshop:
- We propose running the attached 50-sample eval, plus the 5 edge samples Samir will add. Measure: p50/p95 latencies, tokens/sec, and per-inference USD estimate for both 4-bit quantized and fp16 runs.
- We'll instrument an end-to-end trace and share token-level cost breakdown.

Open items we will bring to the call:
- Concrete cost estimate (I attached a first-pass CSV).
- A short runbook for failover: fallback to a smaller-capacity cheaper variant if interactive pool is saturated.
- SOC2/contract questions: ready to loop Legal if you want a pilot DPA.

If that aligns, we'll prep the slot on Tue 15 May 10:00 AM PT and invite our SRE and model ops engineer (Ben).

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering Manager | Redwood Inference
